title: Verify Ctrl+Delete deletes the next word
body:
Question: Windows users expect Ctrl+Delete to mirror Ctrl+Backspace (delete the NEXT word). Does it already work in foreman?

Today encode_key (src/input.rs) sends Ctrl+Delete as ESC[3;5~ (the xterm modifier form via tilde()). Windows Terminal sends the same ESC[3;5~, so this may already work end to end. Verify before changing anything.

Check first (live, isolated build or the running host):
- PowerShell/PSReadLine: type "alpha beta gamma", Home, Ctrl+Right, then foreman send --keys "Ctrl+Delete" and snapshot. Expect "beta" deleted (KillWord).
- Claude Code: same check in the prompt.
- Optionally bash/readline under WSL, where ESC[3;5~ is often unbound (a readline config question, not a foreman bug).

Only if it fails in PSReadLine or Claude Code: compare with the bytes Windows Terminal sends and match them. Don't invent a non-standard sequence (e.g. ESC d) unless WT sends it.

Related: card 56l1al made Ctrl+Backspace send 0x08. Isolated live-test recipe: launch target/agent/debug/foreman.exe with APPDATA=<scratch dir> and FOREMAN_NO_LANDING=1, find its pipe (\\.\pipe\foreman-ctl-<pid>-*), and set FOREMAN_PIPE to it for send/snapshot.

Done when: a documented live result for PSReadLine + Claude Code. If a change was needed: an encode_key unit test + a process_input test.
